passages.title: The Missing Page
passages.text:
ARCHIVIST: You have come for the ledger, I suppose. Everyone does, eventually.
MEERA: I came for the truth, not for paper.
ARCHIVIST: (dryly) Then you are in the wrong building. Truth is rarely filed. What we keep here is whatever somebody once found convenient to record.
MEERA: My grandfather's name is missing from the register of the village school. He taught there for thirty years.
ARCHIVIST: Absence is also a document, madam. Consider who held the pen. A man who is not written down has either been forgotten or been made to be forgotten, and the two are very different crimes.
MEERA: Which one was it?
ARCHIVIST: (turning a page slowly) I am an archivist, not a prophet. But I notice that the pages for that year have been cut out so neatly that one would need a surgeon's patience, or a clerk's guilt, to do it. No dust has settled on the edges. Somebody has visited recently, and not for the first time.
MEERA: You speak as if you knew the clerk.
ARCHIVIST: I have shaved with him every morning for forty years.

passages.title: Governing by Colour
passages.text: Our district administrations have fallen in love with the dashboard. Every school's attendance, every clinic's footfall, every road's kilometres are now reduced to a coloured tile that turns green or red. The appeal is obvious: a tile is quick to read, easy to compare and hard to argue with. But the very qualities that make a dashboard persuasive also make it treacherous. What it can count, it displays; what it cannot count, it quietly drops. A school may show ninety-five percent attendance while its pupils learn little, since presence is measurable and understanding is not. Worse, once a number becomes a target, those judged by it learn to produce the number rather than the outcome, as every teacher who has watched students cram for examinations knows. None of this is an argument for abandoning data. A blind administrator is no better than a deluded one. The remedy is humility: treat every indicator as a question rather than a verdict, and send a human being to visit the green tile before celebrating it. Otherwise we shall end by governing through colour, and the colours, like the maps of old, will be drawn by those who wish to be believed.

passages.title: The Station Clock
passages.text: When I returned to my home town after twenty years, the first thing I noticed was how small the railway station had become. In memory it had been a cathedral of steam and shouting, its porters as large as gods. Now it was a low yellow building with a clock that was wrong in exactly the way I remembered it being wrong, and I felt, absurdly, a flicker of gratitude towards that clock. The tea-seller was new, naturally, yet he poured from a height exactly as the old one had, as though the gesture, rather than the man, were the permanent resident of the platform. I sat on the bench where my father had once instructed me never to look too eager when meeting relatives, and I understood that I had spent half my life obeying advice whose reasons I had forgotten. The town had not shrunk; I had merely acquired a larger scale against which to measure it. That, I suppose, is what adulthood is: not the discovery that the world is smaller than we thought, but the discovery that our thoughts were once smaller than the world required them to be, and, curiously, still are.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?
options: Either of the two roads lead to the town.
Each of the students has submitted a form.
Many a student have failed the test.
Every of the boys was present.
questions.explanation: "Each of" takes a singular verb, so "has submitted" is correct. "Either of" and "many a" also need singular verbs (leads, has failed), and "every" cannot be followed by "of" (it should be "every one of").

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'The report was already submitted, so he ___ it again, but he did it anyway.'
questions.explanation: 'Needn't have + past participle' means an action was done though it was unnecessary. 'Can't have written' denies the possibility that it happened, contradicting 'he did it'; 'shouldn't' and 'mustn't' suggest wrong or forbidden action, not an unnecessary one.

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag: 'Nobody called while I was out, ___?'
questions.explanation: 'Nobody' is treated as negative, so the tag must be positive, and it takes the plural pronoun 'they' in informal standard usage: 'did they?'. A negative tag clashes with the negative statement.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'She is the only one of my cousins who ___ passed the lecturer examination.'
questions.explanation: After 'the only one of', the relative pronoun 'who' refers to 'one' (singular), so 'has' is correct. Compare 'one of those who' where 'who' refers to the plural and takes 'have'.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: "By the time the Chief Guest arrived, the students ___ for two hours."
questions.explanation: A duration before a past point (the arrival) takes the past perfect continuous: "had been waiting". Simple past, past continuous and present perfect continuous do not show duration up to an earlier past moment.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'Hardly ___ the gate when the dog attacked him.'
questions.explanation: After 'hardly' at the start, the auxiliary comes before the subject, and the first action takes the past perfect: 'Hardly had he opened the gate when...'. 'Did he open' wrongly uses the simple past.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Only when the bell rang, the students left.
Only when the bell rang the students did leave.
Only when did the bell ring the students left.
Only when the bell rang did the students leave.
questions.explanation: When a clause beginning with "only when" opens the sentence, the main clause takes subject-auxiliary inversion: "did the students leave". The other options omit the inversion or place it in the wrong clause.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'If I ___ harder in college, I would be holding a better job now.'
questions.explanation: This is a mixed conditional: a past unreal condition (had + past participle) with a present result (would + base verb). 'Would have studied' cannot stand in the if-clause.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'The Board insisted that every candidate ___ present at the venue by 9 a.m.'
questions.explanation: After verbs of insistence, demand or recommendation, the mandative subjunctive uses the base form: 'that every candidate be present'. Indicative forms like 'is' or 'was' are not used.

questions.question: Which sentence implies that the speaker has only one brother?
options: My brother who lives in Pune is a doctor.
My brother that lives in Pune is a doctor.
My brother, who lives in Pune, is a doctor.
The brother who lives in Pune is a doctor.
questions.explanation: A non-defining clause (commas) adds extra information about an already identified person, so it implies only one brother. The defining clauses in the other sentences pick out one brother from several.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'I prefer the white shirts to the blue ___.'
questions.explanation: The substitute word 'ones' replaces the plural noun 'shirts' after the adjective 'blue'. 'One' is singular, while 'it' and 'that' cannot be modified by an adjective in this way.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a dangling modifier?
options: Walking along the beach, the sunset looked beautiful to us.
Walking along the beach, we admired the sunset.
While we were walking along the beach, the sunset looked beautiful.
Having finished the work, she left the office.
questions.explanation: In the first sentence 'Walking along the beach' should describe the person walking, but the subject of the main clause is 'the sunset', so the modifier dangles. In the others the participle matches the subject or a full clause is used.

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect form of: She said, 'I will call you tomorrow if I have time.'
options: She said that she will call me tomorrow if she has time.
She said that she would call me the next day if she had time.
She said that she would call me tomorrow if she had had time.
She said that she will call me the next day if she had time.
questions.explanation: With a past reporting verb, will becomes would, have becomes had (backshift), 'you' becomes 'me' and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'. The other options keep an unshifted verb or add an unjustified past perfect.

questions.question: In the sentence 'The government has clamped down on hoarding', the phrasal verb 'clamped down on' means
questions.explanation: To clamp down on something is to take firm action to stop or restrict it. The other options give the opposite or an unrelated meaning.

questions.question: Convert into a compound sentence: 'Unless you hurry, you will miss the train.'
options: Hurry up, and you will miss the train.
Hurry up, but you will miss the train.
If you hurry, you will miss the train.
Hurry up, or you will miss the train.
questions.explanation: 'Unless you hurry' means 'if you do not hurry', which is expressed in a compound sentence as an imperative joined by 'or': 'Hurry up, or you will miss the train.' The other options change the meaning, and 'If you hurry' is still complex.

questions.question: The Greek root 'chron' in the word 'synchronise' relates to
questions.explanation: Chron- comes from Greek chronos, meaning time (chronology, chronic, synchronise = occur at the same time). Sound is phon-, light is photo-, life is bio-.

questions.question: In which of the following words does the prefix mean 'before'?
questions.explanation: Ante- means before (antecedent = something that goes before). In antibiotic, antidote and antipode the prefix is the Greek anti-, meaning against or opposite.

questions.question: In which sentence does 'fast' carry the sense of 'firmly fixed'?
options: The ship stuck fast in the mud.
She decided to fast on Monday.
His watch is five minutes fast.
questions.explanation: In 'stuck fast', fast means firmly or securely held. In the other sentences it means quick (adverb), to abstain from food (verb) and ahead of the correct time.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: 'The doctor tried to ___ the patient that the operation was routine.'
questions.explanation: Assure means to tell someone confidently so as to remove doubt and takes a person as its object. Ensure means to make certain, insure relates to insurance and assume means to suppose.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: 'The cyclone ___ havoc along the coast.'
questions.explanation: 'Wreak havoc' is the fixed collocation, meaning to cause great damage. 'Wrecked' means ruined and is a common near-homophone error; 'reeked' means smelt strongly.

questions.question: Which word changes from noun to verb when the stress shifts from the first to the second syllable?
questions.explanation: OBject (noun) becomes obJECT (verb). Borrow and finish keep the same stress, and 'advice' is only a noun (the verb is 'advise').

questions.question: Which of the following lexical bundles signals a concession?
questions.explanation: 'Be that as it may' accepts a preceding point while moving on to a contrasting one, i.e. a concession. 'As a result of' and 'on account of' signal cause; 'in order to' signals purpose.

questions.question: The expression 'to cut the Gordian knot' means
options: to solve a complex problem by a bold, decisive stroke
questions.explanation: In legend Alexander severed the impossibly tangled Gordian knot with his sword, so the idiom means solving a difficult problem by a direct, drastic action rather than patient unravelling.

questions.question: A 'Pyrrhic victory' is
options: a victory that benefits only the loser
a victory gained at such a heavy cost that it is almost a defeat
a hollow victory achieved by cheating
questions.explanation: The phrase comes from King Pyrrhus, whose army won against the Romans at terrible cost. It means a win so costly that it is hardly worth it.

questions.question: The idiom 'to bell the cat' means
options: to warn an enemy of danger
to undertake a dangerous task for the benefit of others
questions.explanation: From the fable in which mice plan to hang a bell on the cat's neck, the idiom means to take on a risky task on behalf of a group. It does not mean warning an enemy, punishing or betraying.

questions.question: 'All hands on deck' is an example of
questions.explanation: 'Hands' stands for the sailors as a whole person through a part, which is synecdoche (part for whole). In metonymy the substitute is merely associated with the thing (e.g. 'the crown' for the king).

questions.question: 'He took his hat and his leave.' is an example of
questions.explanation: Zeugma uses one verb ('took') with two objects in different senses: literal (hat) and idiomatic (leave). Oxymoron combines contradictory terms; hyperbole exaggerates; irony says the opposite of what is meant.

questions.question: Identify the figure of speech in: 'He spent a sleepless night.'
questions.explanation: 'Sleepless' describes the person who could not sleep, but it is transferred to the night. This shifting of an adjective to a noun it cannot logically qualify is transferred epithet (hypallage).

questions.question: 'Government of the people, by the people, for the people' repeats the same words at the end of successive clauses. This device is called
questions.explanation: Epistrophe repeats a word or phrase at the end of successive clauses (here 'the people'). Anaphora repeats at the beginning, chiasmus reverses structure and apostrophe addresses an absent person.

questions.question: 'Less is more' is best described as a
questions.explanation: A paradox is a statement that appears self-contradictory yet holds a truth (simplicity can have greater effect). An oxymoron is a compressed two-word contradiction like 'bitter sweet'; a pun plays on word sounds.

questions.question: The archivist's remark, 'Truth is rarely filed', chiefly suggests that
options: records are usually destroyed before the truth can be written down
documents tend to preserve what was convenient for their makers, not necessarily what happened
truth can never be known by anyone
questions.explanation: He adds that the archive keeps 'whatever somebody once found convenient to record', so records reflect the interests of recorders. The passage never says records are destroyed before writing, that truth is unknowable or that the archive is disorderly.

questions.question: 'Absence is also a document' most nearly means that
options: a document that is missing has no value
an archive should keep empty pages
a missing document is more reliable than a written one
what is left out of a record can itself serve as evidence
questions.explanation: The archivist argues that a missing name tells us something about who controlled the record, so the gap is itself evidence. The other options misread the claim as being about value, empty pages or reliability.

questions.question: The last line, 'I have shaved with him every morning for forty years', most plausibly implies that
options: the archivist himself is the clerk who cut the pages
the clerk is the archivist's barber
the clerk died forty years ago
questions.explanation: The person one shares a mirror with every morning is oneself; combined with the clue of the freshly cut pages and the archivist's evasiveness, the line suggests he is the clerk. It is not about a barber, a death or Meera's acquaintances.

questions.question: The archivist's tone in the extract is best described as
options: dry and wry, with an undertone of guilt
questions.explanation: His remarks are dryly witty ('not a prophet', 'surgeon's patience') yet hint at personal guilt, which a dry, wry tone with guilt captures. He is neither angry, cheerful nor confused.

questions.question: Which of the following CANNOT be inferred from the extract?
options: The pages for a particular year were cut out with great care.
The archivist has documentary proof that Meera's grandfather was deliberately erased.
Meera cares more about the truth than about the paper record.
The archivist distinguishes between being forgotten and being made to be forgotten.
questions.explanation: The archivist only notices neatly cut pages; he offers no documentary proof and says he is 'not a prophet'. The other three statements are stated or clearly implied in the dialogue.

questions.question: The central argument of the editorial is that
options: dashboards should be abolished from administration
indicators are useful but should prompt inquiry rather than serve as final verdicts, because what is easily counted can mislead
attendance is the best measure of school quality
questions.explanation: The writer says 'none of this is an argument for abandoning data' and recommends treating each indicator as 'a question rather than a verdict'. The other options distort or contradict this.

questions.question: In the passage, 'treacherous' most nearly means
questions.explanation: The qualities that make dashboards persuasive (speed, simplicity) also mislead, so 'treacherous' means seeming reliable but actually deceiving. The context does not concern physical danger, cruelty or complexity.

questions.question: Which of the following CANNOT be inferred from the editorial?
options: A tile on a dashboard is easy to compare with others.
High attendance does not guarantee learning.
People judged by a figure may begin to produce the figure itself.
The writer wants administrators to stop collecting data.
questions.explanation: The writer explicitly states that none of this is an argument for abandoning data, so wanting collection stopped contradicts the text. The other three are stated directly.

questions.question: The closing comparison with 'the maps of old' chiefly relies on
options: an analogy suggesting that representations can serve the interests of their makers
questions.explanation: Maps of old were drawn to please patrons rather than show reality; likening dashboards to them is an analogy about representation serving its makers. There is no oxymoron or cited authority, and the sentence is not about cartography as such.

questions.question: 'A blind administrator is no better than a deluded one' implies that
options: ignoring data is as unwise as trusting it blindly
questions.explanation: 'Blind' stands for ignoring data and 'deluded' for over-trusting it; the sentence puts both errors on par, justifying the writer's call for balance. The other options misread the metaphor.

questions.question: The narrator feels 'a flicker of gratitude' towards the clock because
options: it made him miss his train
its familiar fault offered continuity with his memory
questions.explanation: The clock was wrong 'in exactly the way I remembered', so its consistency linked the present station to his past. The passage says nothing about its accuracy, a missed train or a new installation.

questions.question: The statement that 'the gesture, rather than the man, were the permanent resident of the platform' suggests that
options: habits and practices can outlast the individuals who perform them
the old tea-seller is still there
the tea-seller is careless about his work
the platform has no permanent staff
questions.explanation: Though the tea-seller is new, he pours exactly as his predecessor did, so the practice persists while the person changes. The narrator expressly says the seller is new.

questions.question: According to the narrator, adulthood is the realisation that
options: the world has actually grown smaller
our earlier understanding was smaller than the world required
questions.explanation: The final sentence defines adulthood as discovering that 'our thoughts were once smaller than the world required them to be'. He explicitly rejects the idea that the world is smaller; the town 'had not shrunk'.

questions.question: The phrase 'a cathedral of steam and shouting' is
options: a metaphor conveying a child's awe
questions.explanation: The station is directly called a cathedral without 'like' or 'as', which makes it a metaphor, and the grandeur reflects childhood awe. It is neither a simile nor an understatement, and nothing is given human traits.

questions.question: Why does the narrator mention his father's advice about not looking eager?
options: To illustrate that he had obeyed advice without remembering its reasons
To blame his father for his shyness
To show that his relatives were hostile
To explain why he missed the train
questions.explanation: The narrator says he understood that he had spent half his life obeying advice whose reasons he had forgotten; the example illustrates this. Blame, hostility or a missed train are not mentioned.

questions.question: According to Krashen's Monitor Hypothesis, which of the following is NOT a condition for the learner to use the Monitor?
questions.questionHi: क्रैशेन की Monitor Hypothesis के अनुसार निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा Monitor के उपयोग की शर्त नहीं है?
questions.explanation: Krashen states that the Monitor (learned knowledge used to edit output) operates only when the performer has enough time, focuses on form and knows the rule. A high affective filter is an obstacle to acquisition, not a condition for Monitor use.
questions.explanationHi: क्रैशेन के अनुसार Monitor (सीखे हुए ज्ञान से अपने उत्पादन को सुधारना) तभी काम करता है जब पर्याप्त समय हो, रूप पर ध्यान हो और नियम पता हो। उच्च भावात्मक अवरोध अर्जन में बाधा है, Monitor के उपयोग की शर्त नहीं।

questions.question: Swain's Output Hypothesis claims that producing language helps acquisition mainly because it
questions.questionHi: स्वेन की Output Hypothesis के अनुसार भाषा का उत्पादन (बोलना/लिखना) अर्जन में मुख्यतः इसलिए सहायक है क्योंकि वह
options: pushes learners to notice the gap between what they want to say and what they can say
optionsHi: विद्यार्थियों को यह देखने के लिए प्रेरित करता है कि वे जो कहना चाहते हैं और जो कह पाते हैं, उसमें अंतर है
बोधगम्य निवेश (comprehensible input) को अनावश्यक बना देता है
भावात्मक अवरोध को कम करता है
यांत्रिक दोहराव से आदतें बनाता है
questions.explanation: Swain argued that 'pushed output' triggers noticing of linguistic gaps, hypothesis-testing and reflection on form. She did not claim input is unnecessary; lowering the filter is Krashen's concern and habit formation is behaviourist.
questions.explanationHi: स्वेन के अनुसार 'pushed output' भाषाई कमियों को पहचानने, परिकल्पना-परीक्षण और रूप पर चिंतन को प्रेरित करता है। उन्होंने निवेश को अनावश्यक नहीं कहा; अवरोध घटाना क्रैशेन का विषय है और आदत-निर्माण व्यवहारवादी विचार है।

questions.question: The role of negotiation of meaning (clarification requests, confirmation checks) in making input comprehensible is central to which hypothesis?
questions.questionHi: अर्थ-वार्ता (negotiation of meaning), जैसे स्पष्टीकरण के अनुरोध और पुष्टि-जाँच, द्वारा निवेश को बोधगम्य बनाना किस परिकल्पना का केंद्रीय विचार है?
questions.explanation: Michael Long's Interaction Hypothesis says that conversational interaction in which learners negotiate meaning makes input comprehensible and promotes acquisition. The other three are Krashen's hypotheses with different concerns.
questions.explanationHi: माइकल लॉन्ग की Interaction Hypothesis कहती है कि जिस वार्तालाप में विद्यार्थी अर्थ की वार्ता करते हैं, उससे निवेश बोधगम्य बनता है और अर्जन बढ़ता है। शेष तीन क्रैशेन की परिकल्पनाएँ हैं जिनके सरोकार भिन्न हैं।

questions.question: The argument that children master complex grammar despite limited and imperfect input, supporting the idea of innate linguistic knowledge, is known as
questions.questionHi: यह तर्क कि बच्चे सीमित और अपूर्ण निवेश के बावजूद जटिल व्याकरण सीख लेते हैं, जो जन्मजात भाषाई ज्ञान का समर्थन करता है, कहलाता है
options: the poverty of the stimulus argument
optionsHi: उद्दीपन की निर्धनता (poverty of the stimulus) का तर्क
questions.explanation: Chomsky argued that the input children hear is too sparse and error-ridden to explain their grammatical knowledge, so some of it must be innate (the LAD). Reinforcement is Skinner, ZPD is Vygotsky and fossilisation concerns second-language plateaus.
questions.explanationHi: चॉम्स्की के अनुसार बच्चों को मिलने वाला निवेश इतना कम और त्रुटिपूर्ण है कि उससे उनका व्याकरणिक ज्ञान समझाया नहीं जा सकता, इसलिए कुछ ज्ञान जन्मजात (LAD) होना चाहिए। पुनर्बलन स्किनर से, ZPD वाइगोत्स्की से और जीवाश्मीकरण द्वितीय भाषा के ठहराव से जुड़ा है।

questions.question: An immigrant child chats fluently with friends in English but struggles with the science textbook. In Cummins' terms,
questions.questionHi: एक प्रवासी बच्चा मित्रों से अंग्रेज़ी में धाराप्रवाह बातचीत करता है पर विज्ञान की पाठ्यपुस्तक में कठिनाई महसूस करता है। कमिन्स की शब्दावली में,
options: both BICS and CALP are fully developed
CALP is developed but BICS is not
neither BICS nor CALP has begun
BICS is developed but CALP is not yet
optionsHi: BICS और CALP दोनों पूर्ण विकसित हैं
CALP विकसित है पर BICS नहीं
BICS और CALP दोनों शुरू ही नहीं हुए
BICS विकसित है पर CALP अभी नहीं
questions.explanation: BICS (Basic Interpersonal Communicative Skills) are conversational skills gained in about two years; CALP (Cognitive Academic Language Proficiency), needed for textbooks and abstract thought, takes about five to seven years. The child shows BICS but weak CALP.
questions.explanationHi: BICS (बुनियादी पारस्परिक संवाद कौशल) बोलचाल के कौशल हैं जो लगभग दो वर्ष में आ जाते हैं; CALP (संज्ञानात्मक-शैक्षिक भाषा दक्षता), जो पाठ्यपुस्तक और अमूर्त चिंतन के लिए चाहिए, में लगभग पाँच से सात वर्ष लगते हैं। बच्चे में BICS है पर CALP कमज़ोर है।

questions.question: A child asks, 'Why does it rain?' Which of Halliday's early functions of language does this illustrate?
questions.questionHi: एक बच्चा पूछता है, 'बारिश क्यों होती है?' यह हैलिडे के भाषा के किस प्रारंभिक प्रकार्य (function) को दर्शाता है?
questions.explanation: The heuristic function uses language to explore and learn about the environment, as with 'why' questions. Regulatory controls others' behaviour, instrumental satisfies needs and imaginative creates imaginary worlds.
questions.explanationHi: अन्वेषणात्मक (heuristic) प्रकार्य में भाषा से वातावरण को जानने-सीखने का प्रयास होता है, जैसे 'क्यों' वाले प्रश्न। नियामक दूसरों के व्यवहार को नियंत्रित करता है, साधनात्मक आवश्यकताएँ पूरी करता है और कल्पनात्मक काल्पनिक संसार रचता है।

questions.question: A learner forgets a word and uses a paraphrase to keep communicating. Which component of Canale and Swain's communicative competence is this?
questions.questionHi: कोई विद्यार्थी शब्द भूल जाता है और संवाद जारी रखने के लिए पर्यायोक्ति (paraphrase) का प्रयोग करता है। यह कैनेल और स्वेन की संप्रेषणात्मक सक्षमता (communicative competence) का कौन-सा घटक है?
questions.explanation: Strategic competence is the ability to use compensation strategies such as paraphrase, gestures or circumlocution to repair communication breakdowns. Grammatical concerns accuracy, discourse concerns coherence and sociolinguistic concerns appropriateness.
questions.explanationHi: रणनीतिक सक्षमता वह योग्यता है जिसमें पर्यायोक्ति, हाव-भाव या घुमा-फिराकर कहने जैसी क्षतिपूर्ति युक्तियों से संवाद की बाधा दूर की जाती है। व्याकरणिक सक्षमता शुद्धता से, प्रवचन सक्षमता संगति से और सामाजिक-भाषावैज्ञानिक सक्षमता उपयुक्तता से जुड़ी है।

questions.question: A learner says 'goed' and 'foots', applying regular rules to irregular forms. Error analysis classifies these as
questions.questionHi: एक विद्यार्थी 'goed' और 'foots' कहता है, यानी अनियमित रूपों पर नियमित नियम लगाता है। त्रुटि-विश्लेषण (error analysis) इन्हें किस श्रेणी में रखता है?
options: interlingual errors caused by L1 transfer
optionsHi: मातृभाषा-अंतरण (L1 transfer) से उत्पन्न अंतर-भाषिक त्रुटियाँ
questions.explanation: 'Goed' and 'foots' arise from the target language's own rules being over-applied, which is overgeneralisation, a type of intralingual (developmental) error. They are not L1 transfer, random slips or necessarily fossilised.
questions.explanationHi: 'Goed' और 'foots' लक्ष्य-भाषा के ही नियमों को अधिक लागू करने से बनते हैं, जो अति-सामान्यीकरण है और अंतःभाषिक (विकासात्मक) त्रुटि का प्रकार है। ये L1 अंतरण, आकस्मिक चूक या अनिवार्यतः जीवाश्मीकृत त्रुटियाँ नहीं हैं।

questions.question: Selinker's term 'fossilisation' refers to
questions.questionHi: सेलिंकर का शब्द 'जीवाश्मीकरण' (fossilisation) किसे कहते हैं?
options: the gradual disappearance of the first language
the silent period of a beginner
the permanent stagnation of certain non-target forms in a learner's interlanguage despite continued exposure
optionsHi: प्रथम भाषा का धीरे-धीरे लुप्त होना
आरंभिक सीखने वाले की मौन अवधि
लगातार संपर्क के बावजूद अधिगमकर्ता की अंतर्भाषा (interlanguage) में कुछ अशुद्ध रूपों का स्थायी रूप से ठहर जाना
questions.explanation: Fossilisation is the permanent stabilisation of incorrect forms in the interlanguage even after long exposure and instruction. It is unrelated to L1 attrition, the silent period or fast idiom learning.
questions.explanationHi: जीवाश्मीकरण में लंबे संपर्क और शिक्षण के बाद भी अंतर्भाषा में अशुद्ध रूप स्थायी रूप से जम जाते हैं। इसका संबंध L1 के क्षय, मौन अवधि या मुहावरों के तेज़ अर्जन से नहीं है।

questions.question: In the Anderson-Krathwohl revised Bloom's taxonomy, which cognitive process is placed at the highest level, e.g. writing an original short story?
questions.questionHi: एंडरसन-क्रैथवोहल के संशोधित ब्लूम वर्गीकरण में सर्वोच्च स्तर पर कौन-सी संज्ञानात्मक प्रक्रिया है, जैसे मौलिक लघुकथा लिखना?
questions.explanation: The revised taxonomy runs Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyse, Evaluate, Create, with Create at the top, where learners put elements together to produce something original. In the original taxonomy, Evaluation was the top level.
questions.explanationHi: संशोधित वर्गीकरण का क्रम है: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyse, Evaluate, Create; सबसे ऊपर Create है, जहाँ विद्यार्थी तत्वों को जोड़कर कुछ मौलिक रचते हैं। मूल वर्गीकरण में सर्वोच्च स्तर Evaluation था।

questions.question: Which classroom practice best illustrates scaffolding in a writing lesson?
questions.questionHi: लेखन के पाठ में कौन-सी कक्षा-गतिविधि स्कैफ़ोल्डिंग (scaffolding) का सबसे अच्छा उदाहरण है?
options: Giving a finished essay for students to copy
Providing sentence frames and a model paragraph, then gradually withdrawing them as students gain confidence
Leaving students to write without any help to promote discovery
Correcting every error in red ink
optionsHi: विद्यार्थियों को नकल करने के लिए तैयार निबंध देना
वाक्य-ढाँचे और आदर्श अनुच्छेद देना और आत्मविश्वास बढ़ने पर उन्हें धीरे-धीरे हटाना
खोज को बढ़ावा देने के लिए बिना किसी सहायता के लिखने देना
हर त्रुटि को लाल स्याही से सुधारना
questions.explanation: Scaffolding (Bruner, drawing on Vygotsky's ZPD) is temporary, adjustable support that is gradually withdrawn. Copying gives no growth, no help ignores the ZPD and heavy correction is not support in doing the task.
questions.explanationHi: स्कैफ़ोल्डिंग (ब्रूनर, वाइगोत्स्की के ZPD पर आधारित) अस्थायी, समायोज्य सहायता है जिसे धीरे-धीरे हटाया जाता है। नकल से विकास नहीं होता, बिना सहायता के छोड़ना ZPD की उपेक्षा है और भारी सुधार कार्य करने में सहायता नहीं है।

questions.question: In Willis's Task-Based Language Teaching framework, the stages of a lesson are, in order,
questions.questionHi: विलिस के कार्य-आधारित भाषा शिक्षण (TBLT) ढाँचे में पाठ के चरण क्रमशः हैं
optionsHi: पूर्व-कार्य, कार्य-चक्र, भाषा-केंद्रण (Pre-task, Task cycle, Language focus)
questions.explanation: Willis proposed Pre-task (introducing topic and task), Task cycle (task, planning, report) and then Language focus (analysis and practice of forms). Presentation-Practice-Production is the traditional structural lesson order.
questions.explanationHi: विलिस के अनुसार पहले Pre-task (विषय और कार्य का परिचय), फिर Task cycle (कार्य, योजना, रिपोर्ट) और अंत में Language focus (रूपों का विश्लेषण व अभ्यास) आता है। Presentation-Practice-Production पारंपरिक संरचनात्मक पाठ-क्रम है।

questions.question: Allowing learners to draw flexibly on all their languages, e.g. discussing in Hindi before writing in English, reflects
questions.questionHi: विद्यार्थियों को अपनी सभी भाषाओं का लचीले ढंग से उपयोग करने देना, जैसे अंग्रेज़ी में लिखने से पहले हिंदी में चर्चा करना, किसे दर्शाता है?
options: the Direct Method's ban on the mother tongue
translanguaging as a multilingual classroom strategy
optionsHi: प्रत्यक्ष विधि द्वारा मातृभाषा पर प्रतिबंध
बहुभाषी कक्षा की रणनीति के रूप में ट्रांसलैंग्वेजिंग (translanguaging)
questions.explanation: Translanguaging treats a learner's languages as one resource and uses them together to make meaning. The Direct Method avoids L1, the Audio-lingual method builds habits through drills and contrastive analysis compares language systems.
questions.explanationHi: ट्रांसलैंग्वेजिंग में विद्यार्थी की सभी भाषाओं को एक संसाधन मानकर अर्थ-निर्माण में साथ-साथ प्रयोग किया जाता है। प्रत्यक्ष विधि L1 से बचती है, श्रव्य-भाषिक विधि अभ्यास से आदत बनाती है और विरोधात्मक विश्लेषण भाषा-प्रणालियों की तुलना करता है।

questions.question: Effective remedial teaching in English should begin with
questions.questionHi: अंग्रेज़ी में प्रभावी उपचारात्मक शिक्षण (remedial teaching) की शुरुआत किससे होनी चाहिए?
options: diagnosing the nature and cause of learners' difficulties from their error patterns
giving extra homework of the same type
moving weak learners to a separate class
optionsHi: त्रुटि-प्रतिमानों से विद्यार्थियों की कठिनाइयों की प्रकृति और कारण का निदान करने से
उसी प्रकार का अतिरिक्त गृहकार्य देने से
कमज़ोर विद्यार्थियों को अलग कक्षा में भेजने से
questions.explanation: Remedial work must follow diagnosis: identify what the errors are and why they occur, then design targeted activities. Blind repetition, extra homework or segregation does not address the actual difficulty.
questions.explanationHi: उपचारात्मक कार्य निदान के बाद ही होना चाहिए: पहले पहचानें कि त्रुटियाँ क्या हैं और क्यों होती हैं, फिर लक्षित गतिविधियाँ बनाएँ। अंधाधुंध दोहराव, अतिरिक्त गृहकार्य या अलग करना वास्तविक कठिनाई को नहीं सुलझाता।

questions.question: Bruner's 'Language Acquisition Support System' (LASS), proposed as a complement to Chomsky's LAD, refers to
questions.questionHi: चॉम्स्की के LAD के पूरक के रूप में ब्रूनर द्वारा प्रस्तावित 'भाषा अर्जन सहायता प्रणाली' (LASS) किसे कहते हैं?
options: an innate grammar module in the brain
the interactive social support from caregivers, such as routines and formats, that helps the child learn language
optionsHi: देखभाल करने वालों द्वारा दिया जाने वाला अंतःक्रियात्मक सामाजिक सहारा, जैसे दिनचर्याएँ और ढाँचे, जो बच्चे को भाषा सीखने में मदद करता है
questions.explanation: Bruner argued that caregiver-child interaction in familiar routines (games, feeding, picture-book reading) scaffolds language learning, supplementing the innate LAD. It is a social support system, not an innate module, drill or test.
questions.explanationHi: ब्रूनर के अनुसार परिचित दिनचर्याओं (खेल, भोजन, चित्र-पुस्तक पढ़ना) में देखभालकर्ता और बच्चे की अंतःक्रिया भाषा-अधिगम को सहारा देती है और जन्मजात LAD की पूरक है। यह सामाजिक सहायता प्रणाली है, न कि जन्मजात मॉड्यूल, अभ्यास या परीक्षण।

questions.question: A student refrains from cheating because "my teacher and family would think badly of me". At which Kohlberg stage is this reasoning?
questions.questionHi: एक विद्यार्थी नकल से इसलिए बचता है कि "मेरे शिक्षक और परिवार मेरे बारे में बुरा सोचेंगे"। यह तर्क कोहलबर्ग के किस चरण का है?
questions.explanation: Seeking the approval of others and being seen as a good person is Stage 3, in the conventional level. Stage 1 fears punishment, Stage 2 seeks personal gain and Stage 5 reasons from social contract and rights.
questions.explanationHi: दूसरों की स्वीकृति पाना और अच्छा व्यक्ति दिखना चरण 3 है, जो परंपरागत स्तर में आता है। चरण 1 में दंड का भय, चरण 2 में व्यक्तिगत लाभ तथा चरण 5 में सामाजिक अनुबंध और अधिकारों का तर्क होता है।

questions.question: According to Erikson, the psychosocial crisis of 'industry versus inferiority' is typically faced during
questions.questionHi: एरिक्सन के अनुसार 'उद्यमशीलता बनाम हीनता' (industry versus inferiority) का मनो-सामाजिक संकट सामान्यतः किस अवस्था में आता है?
questions.explanation: Children of about 6–12 years learn skills at school; success gives a sense of industry, failure gives inferiority. Trust vs mistrust belongs to infancy, autonomy vs shame to early childhood and identity vs role confusion to adolescence.
questions.explanationHi: लगभग 6–12 वर्ष के बच्चे विद्यालय में कौशल सीखते हैं; सफलता से उद्यमशीलता और असफलता से हीनता की भावना बनती है। विश्वास बनाम अविश्वास शैशव का, स्वायत्तता बनाम लज्जा प्रारंभिक बाल्यावस्था का तथा पहचान बनाम भूमिका-भ्रम किशोरावस्था का संकट है।

questions.question: In Piaget's sensorimotor stage, 'tertiary circular reactions', in which the infant deliberately varies actions to see new results, appear at about
questions.questionHi: पियाजे की संवेदी-गामक अवस्था में 'तृतीयक वृत्तीय प्रतिक्रियाएँ' (tertiary circular reactions), जिनमें शिशु नए परिणाम देखने के लिए जान-बूझकर क्रियाएँ बदलता है, लगभग कब दिखती हैं?
questions.explanation: Tertiary circular reactions (the 'little scientist' experimenting) belong to the fifth sub-stage, about 12–18 months. Reflexes are 0–1 month, primary circular reactions 1–4 months and secondary circular reactions 4–8 months.
questions.explanationHi: तृतीयक वृत्तीय प्रतिक्रियाएँ ('छोटा वैज्ञानिक' बनकर प्रयोग करना) पाँचवीं उप-अवस्था में, लगभग 12–18 माह पर आती हैं। सहज क्रियाएँ 0–1 माह, प्राथमिक वृत्तीय 1–4 माह तथा द्वितीयक वृत्तीय 4–8 माह में होती हैं।

questions.question: A child who learns best by classifying plants, animals and rocks and enjoys nature walks shows strength in which of Gardner's intelligences?
questions.questionHi: एक बच्चा पौधों, पशुओं और चट्टानों का वर्गीकरण करके सबसे अच्छा सीखता है और प्रकृति-भ्रमण पसंद करता है। यह गार्डनर की किस बुद्धि में सबल है?
questions.explanation: Naturalistic intelligence is the ability to recognise and classify elements of the natural world. Interpersonal concerns understanding people, logical-mathematical concerns reasoning with numbers and bodily-kinaesthetic concerns movement skills.
questions.explanationHi: प्राकृतिक बुद्धि प्रकृति के तत्वों को पहचानने और वर्गीकृत करने की योग्यता है। अंतर्वैयक्तिक बुद्धि लोगों को समझने से, तार्किक-गणितीय संख्याओं से तर्क करने से और शारीरिक-गतिक गतिशील कौशलों से संबंधित है।

questions.question: A person's vocabulary and general knowledge, which usually keep growing even in old age, mainly reflect
questions.questionHi: किसी व्यक्ति की शब्दावली और सामान्य जानकारी, जो प्रायः वृद्धावस्था तक बढ़ती रहती है, मुख्यतः किसे दर्शाती है?
questions.explanation: Cattell's crystallised intelligence is accumulated knowledge and skills from experience and education and keeps growing with age, whereas fluid intelligence (novel reasoning, speed) tends to decline after early adulthood.
questions.explanationHi: कैटेल की स्फटिकीकृत बुद्धि अनुभव और शिक्षा से संचित ज्ञान व कौशल है, जो आयु के साथ बढ़ती रहती है; जबकि तरल बुद्धि (नई समस्याओं का तर्क, गति) प्रारंभिक वयस्कता के बाद घटने लगती है।

questions.question: Which of the following tasks best measures divergent thinking?
questions.questionHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कार्य अपसारी चिंतन (divergent thinking) को सबसे अच्छी तरह मापता है?
options: Finding the single correct answer to an arithmetic problem
Listing as many unusual uses of a brick as possible
Recalling the date of a historical event
optionsHi: अंकगणित के प्रश्न का एक सही उत्तर निकालना
ईंट के अधिक से अधिक असामान्य उपयोग सूचीबद्ध करना
किसी ऐतिहासिक घटना की तिथि याद करना
questions.explanation: Divergent thinking (Guilford, Torrance) generates many varied, original responses to an open problem, scored on fluency, flexibility and originality. The other tasks need one correct answer, i.e. convergent thinking or recall.
questions.explanationHi: अपसारी चिंतन (गिलफोर्ड, टॉरेंस) में खुली समस्या के अनेक, विविध और मौलिक उत्तर दिए जाते हैं, जिन्हें प्रवाह, लचीलेपन और मौलिकता पर आँका जाता है। अन्य कार्यों में एक ही सही उत्तर चाहिए, अर्थात ये अभिसारी चिंतन या स्मरण हैं।

questions.question: The split-half method, corrected with the Spearman-Brown formula, estimates which type of reliability?
questions.questionHi: स्पीयरमैन-ब्राउन सूत्र से संशोधित अर्ध-विभाजन (split-half) विधि किस प्रकार की विश्वसनीयता का आकलन करती है?
questions.explanation: Both halves of a single test are correlated and the coefficient is stepped up to full length with Spearman-Brown, giving internal consistency. Test-retest needs two administrations; parallel forms need two equivalent tests.
questions.explanationHi: एक ही परीक्षण के दोनों भागों का सहसंबंध निकालकर स्पीयरमैन-ब्राउन से पूरी लंबाई के लिए संशोधित किया जाता है, जिससे आंतरिक संगति मिलती है। test-retest में दो बार परीक्षण और समानांतर रूप में दो समतुल्य परीक्षण चाहिए।

questions.question: An item has a discrimination index of −0.20. This indicates that
questions.questionHi: किसी प्रश्न का विभेदन सूचकांक (discrimination index) −0.20 है। इससे संकेत मिलता है कि
options: weaker students answered it correctly more often than stronger students, so it should be revised or dropped
the item discriminates well between high and low achievers
optionsHi: कमज़ोर विद्यार्थियों ने मज़बूत विद्यार्थियों से अधिक बार सही उत्तर दिया, इसलिए प्रश्न को सुधारना या हटाना चाहिए
प्रश्न उच्च और निम्न उपलब्धि वाले विद्यार्थियों में अच्छा भेद करता है
questions.explanation: A negative discrimination index means the lower group outperformed the upper group on the item, which signals a flawed item (ambiguous key or misleading wording). Ease is shown by the difficulty index, not by this value.
questions.explanationHi: ऋणात्मक विभेदन सूचकांक का अर्थ है कि निम्न समूह ने उच्च समूह से बेहतर किया, जो प्रश्न में दोष (अस्पष्ट उत्तर-कुंजी या भ्रामक शब्दावली) दर्शाता है। आसानी कठिनाई सूचकांक से पता चलती है, इस मान से नहीं।

questions.question: A teacher checks that her English achievement test samples every unit of the syllabus in proportion to its weightage. She is establishing
questions.questionHi: एक शिक्षिका जाँचती है कि उसके अंग्रेज़ी उपलब्धि परीक्षण में पाठ्यक्रम की हर इकाई उसके भारांश के अनुपात में शामिल है। वह किसे स्थापित कर रही है?
questions.explanation: Content validity is the extent to which a test adequately and representatively samples the syllabus content, which a blueprint ensures. Predictive validity compares scores with later performance; construct validity concerns the underlying trait.
questions.explanationHi: विषय-वस्तु वैधता वह है जिसमें परीक्षण पाठ्यक्रम की सामग्री का पर्याप्त और प्रतिनिधिक प्रतिदर्श लेता है, जिसे ब्लूप्रिंट सुनिश्चित करता है। भविष्यसूचक वैधता अंकों की बाद के निष्पादन से तुलना करती है; संप्रत्यय वैधता अंतर्निहित गुण से संबंधित है।

questions.question: Which of the following is a defining feature of the Holistic Progress Card proposed under NEP 2020?
questions.questionHi: NEP 2020 में प्रस्तावित समग्र प्रगति पत्रक (Holistic Progress Card) की निर्णायक विशेषता निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी है?
options: Only the final-examination marks of the pupil
Only a class rank based on rote recall
A 360-degree record combining self-assessment, peer assessment and teacher assessment
Only the teacher's remarks on discipline
optionsHi: विद्यार्थी के केवल अंतिम परीक्षा के अंक
स्व-आकलन, सहपाठी-आकलन और शिक्षक-आकलन को मिलाकर 360-डिग्री अभिलेख
अनुशासन पर शिक्षक की केवल टिप्पणियाँ
questions.explanation: The Holistic Progress Card is a 360-degree, multidimensional report covering cognitive, affective and psychomotor domains with inputs from the student, peers, teachers and parents. It is not a marks-only or rank-only document.
questions.explanationHi: समग्र प्रगति पत्रक एक 360-डिग्री, बहुआयामी रिपोर्ट है जो संज्ञानात्मक, भावात्मक और मनो-गामक क्षेत्रों को विद्यार्थी, सहपाठियों, शिक्षकों और अभिभावकों के योगदान सहित दर्शाती है। यह केवल अंकों या रैंक का दस्तावेज़ नहीं है।

questions.question: In the 5E instructional model, the stage in which learners apply the new concept to a fresh situation is called
questions.questionHi: 5E शिक्षण मॉडल में वह चरण, जिसमें विद्यार्थी नई अवधारणा को किसी नई परिस्थिति में लागू करते हैं, कहलाता है
questions.explanation: The five Es are Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate and Evaluate. In Elaborate, learners extend and apply the concept to new contexts; Engage arouses curiosity, Explore gives hands-on experience and Explain formalises the idea.
questions.explanationHi: पाँच E हैं: Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate और Evaluate। Elaborate में विद्यार्थी अवधारणा को नए संदर्भों में लागू करते हैं; Engage जिज्ञासा जगाता है, Explore प्रत्यक्ष अनुभव देता है और Explain विचार को औपचारिक रूप देता है।

questions.question: In the NCF for School Education 2023, the 'Preparatory Stage' corresponds to which age group?
questions.questionHi: स्कूली शिक्षा के लिए NCF 2023 में 'प्रारंभिक (Preparatory) चरण' किस आयु-वर्ग से संबंधित है?
questions.explanation: NCF-SE 2023 follows the 5+3+3+4 design: Foundational (ages 3–8), Preparatory (8–11), Middle (11–14) and Secondary (14–18).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the guiding principles of the National Curriculum Framework 2005?
questions.questionHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा राष्ट्रीय पाठ्यचर्या की रूपरेखा 2005 का मार्गदर्शक सिद्धांत नहीं है?
options: Making the textbook the primary and sole source of knowledge
Connecting knowledge to life outside the school
Shifting learning away from rote methods
Making examinations more flexible and integrated with classroom life
optionsHi: पाठ्यपुस्तक को ज्ञान का प्राथमिक और एकमात्र स्रोत बनाना
ज्ञान को विद्यालय के बाहर के जीवन से जोड़ना
अधिगम को रटने की पद्धति से दूर ले जाना
परीक्षाओं को अधिक लचीला और कक्षा-जीवन से जुड़ा बनाना
questions.explanation: NCF 2005 wants curriculum enriched beyond the textbook, so treating the textbook as the sole source contradicts it. The other three are among its five stated guiding principles.
questions.explanationHi: NCF 2005 पाठ्यचर्या को पाठ्यपुस्तक से आगे समृद्ध बनाना चाहता है, इसलिए पाठ्यपुस्तक को एकमात्र स्रोत मानना इसके विरुद्ध है। अन्य तीन इसके पाँच मार्गदर्शक सिद्धांतों में शामिल हैं।

questions.question: In a constructivist classroom, a learner's error is best treated as
questions.questionHi: रचनावादी कक्षा में विद्यार्थी की त्रुटि को सबसे उचित रूप में किस प्रकार देखा जाना चाहिए?
options: a sign of laziness to be punished
a window into the learner's current thinking that guides further teaching
a reason to repeat the lesson in the same manner
optionsHi: आलस्य का संकेत, जिसे दंडित किया जाए
विद्यार्थी की वर्तमान सोच की झलक, जो आगे के शिक्षण को दिशा देती है
पाठ को उसी तरीके से दोहराने का कारण
questions.explanation: Constructivism holds that learners build knowledge from prior ideas, so errors reveal their partial or alternative conceptions and give the teacher a basis for guiding them. Punishing or merely repeating ignores this.
questions.explanationHi: रचनावाद के अनुसार विद्यार्थी पूर्व विचारों से ज्ञान गढ़ते हैं, इसलिए त्रुटियाँ उनकी अधूरी या वैकल्पिक धारणाएँ बताती हैं और शिक्षक को मार्गदर्शन का आधार देती हैं। दंड देना या उसी तरह दोहराना इसे नज़रअंदाज़ करता है।

questions.question: A textbook consistently shows men as doctors and pilots and women only as nurses and homemakers. This is best described as
questions.questionHi: एक पाठ्यपुस्तक में लगातार पुरुषों को डॉक्टर और पायलट तथा महिलाओं को केवल नर्स और गृहिणी दिखाया गया है। इसे सबसे सही रूप में क्या कहा जाएगा?
options: gender stereotyping transmitted through the hidden curriculum
optionsHi: छिपे पाठ्यक्रम (hidden curriculum) के माध्यम से फैलाई गई लैंगिक रूढ़िबद्ध धारणा
questions.explanation: Such repeated role portrayals silently teach children what each gender 'should' do, which is gender stereotyping conveyed by the hidden curriculum. Gender-sensitive education demands balanced, non-stereotypical representation.
questions.explanationHi: ऐसी बार-बार दिखाई गई भूमिकाएँ बच्चों को चुपचाप सिखाती हैं कि हर लिंग को क्या करना 'चाहिए', जो छिपे पाठ्यक्रम से फैली लैंगिक रूढ़िबद्धता है। लिंग-संवेदनशील शिक्षा में संतुलित, रूढ़ि-मुक्त प्रस्तुति आवश्यक है।

questions.question: 'सदैव' शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या है?
questions.explanation: 'सदा' के अंतिम 'आ' और 'एव' के 'ए' के मेल से 'ऐ' बनता है (आ + ए = ऐ), यह वृद्धि संधि है। इसलिए सही विच्छेद 'सदा + एव' है; अन्य विकल्पों में स्वर/व्यंजन गलत टूटे हैं।

questions.question: 'महर्षि' का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या है?
questions.explanation: 'आ' और 'ऋ' के मेल से 'अर्' बनता है (आ + ऋ = अर्), यह गुण संधि है। अतः महा + ऋषि = महर्षि। अन्य विकल्पों में पद या वर्ण गलत हैं।

questions.question: 'गूलर का फूल होना' मुहावरे का अर्थ क्या है?
questions.explanation: गूलर के फूल प्रायः दिखाई नहीं देते, इसलिए जो व्यक्ति या वस्तु बहुत कम या कभी दिखाई न दे उसके लिए 'गूलर का फूल होना' कहा जाता है। इसका सौंदर्य, प्रसन्नता या सुगंध से संबंध नहीं है।

questions.question: 'कनक' शब्द के दो अर्थ कौन-से हैं?
questions.explanation: 'कनक' के प्रमुख अर्थ सोना (स्वर्ण) और धतूरा हैं (साथ ही गेहूँ भी कहा जाता है)। इसलिए पहला विकल्प ही दोनों अर्थों को सही रूप में देता है; शेष विकल्प असंगत हैं।

questions.question: निम्नलिखित में तत्सम–तद्भव की सही जोड़ी कौन-सी है?
questions.explanation: 'स्वप्न' तत्सम है और उसका तद्भव रूप 'सपना' है। 'हस्त' का तद्भव 'हाथ' है (हाथी नहीं), 'सप्त' का 'सात' है, और 'कर्पूर' तत्सम तथा 'कपूर' तद्भव है, इसलिए अंतिम जोड़ी क्रम में उल्टी है।

questions.question: Choose one word for: 'government by the rich'.
questions.explanation: Plutocracy (from Greek ploutos, wealth) is rule by the wealthy. Oligarchy is rule by a few, theocracy is rule by religious authority and aristocracy is rule by a noble or best-born class.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: 'He is senior ___ me by five years.'
questions.explanation: Adjectives like senior, junior, superior, inferior and prior take 'to', not 'than'. So 'senior to me' is correct.

questions.question: Find the part with an error: 'The number of applicants (A) / for the post (B) / have increased (C) / this year (D).'
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb (the subject is 'number'), so it should be 'has increased'. ('A number of' would take a plural verb.)

questions.question: The idiom 'to eat humble pie' means
options: to admit one's mistake humbly and apologise
questions.explanation: To eat humble pie is to submit to humiliation by admitting an error and apologising. It has nothing to do with cooking or pride.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive form of: 'People say that he is honest.'
options: He is said to be honest.
He was said to be honest.
It is said him to be honest.
questions.explanation: For reporting verbs like say, the personal passive is 'He is said to be honest' (present simple, so 'is said'). 'Was said' changes the tense; the other options are ungrammatical.

questions.question: Find the next term: 3, 10, 6, 20, 12, 40, ?
questions.explanation: Two interleaved series: 3, 6, 12, … (×2) and 10, 20, 40, … (×2). The next term belongs to the first series: 12 × 2 = 24.

questions.question: If FRIEND is coded as HUMJTK, how is CANDLE coded in the same way?
questions.questionHi: यदि FRIEND को HUMJTK लिखा जाता है, तो इसी प्रकार CANDLE को कैसे लिखा जाएगा?
questions.explanation: Letters move forward by +2, +3, +4, +5, +6, +7 (F→H, R→U, I→M, E→J, N→T, D→K). Applying this to CANDLE: C→E, A→D, N→R, D→I, L→R, E→L = EDRIRL.
questions.explanationHi: अक्षर क्रमशः +2, +3, +4, +5, +6, +7 आगे बढ़ते हैं (F→H, R→U, I→M, E→J, N→T, D→K)। CANDLE पर लगाने पर C→E, A→D, N→R, D→I, L→R, E→L, यानी EDRIRL।

questions.question: Pointing to a man, Rekha said, 'His mother's only brother is the father of my husband.' How is the man related to Rekha?
questions.questionHi: एक पुरुष की ओर संकेत करते हुए रेखा ने कहा, 'उसकी माँ का इकलौता भाई मेरे पति का पिता है।' वह पुरुष रेखा से किस प्रकार संबंधित है?
questions.explanation: The man's maternal uncle is Rekha's father-in-law. So the man's mother is the sister of Rekha's father-in-law, i.e. the husband's paternal aunt. The man is that aunt's son, hence the husband's cousin.
questions.explanationHi: पुरुष का मामा रेखा का ससुर है। अतः पुरुष की माँ रेखा के ससुर की बहन, यानी पति की बुआ है। पुरुष उस बुआ का पुत्र है, इसलिए पति का फुफेरा भाई (cousin) है।

questions.question:
Statements: Some pens are books. No book is a pencil.
Conclusions: I. Some pens are not pencils. II. No pen is a pencil.
questions.questionHi:
कथन: कुछ पेन किताबें हैं। कोई किताब पेंसिल नहीं है।
निष्कर्ष: I. कुछ पेन पेंसिल नहीं हैं। II. कोई पेन पेंसिल नहीं है।
optionsHi: I और II दोनों अनुसरण करते हैं
न I न II अनुसरण करता है
questions.explanation: The pens that are books cannot be pencils, so some pens are not pencils (I follows). Nothing is known about the other pens, so 'no pen is a pencil' (II) cannot be concluded.
questions.explanationHi: जो पेन किताबें हैं वे पेंसिल नहीं हो सकते, इसलिए कुछ पेन पेंसिल नहीं हैं (I सही)। बाकी पेनों के बारे में कुछ ज्ञात नहीं, अतः 'कोई पेन पेंसिल नहीं' (II) निकाला नहीं जा सकता।

questions.question: Ravi walks 9 km north, then 12 km east, then 4 km south. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.questionHi: रवि 9 किमी उत्तर, फिर 12 किमी पूर्व, फिर 4 किमी दक्षिण चलता है। वह अपने आरंभिक बिंदु से कितनी दूर है?
questions.explanation: Net north displacement = 9 − 4 = 5 km; east = 12 km. Distance = √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 km.

questions.question: What does the formula =COUNTIF(B2:B11,">=40") return?
questions.questionHi: सूत्र =COUNTIF(B2:B11,">=40") क्या परिणाम देता है?
options: The sum of all values that are at least 40 in B2:B11
The average of the values in B2:B11
The number of cells in B2:B11 whose value is 40 or more
optionsHi: B2:B11 में 40 या उससे अधिक सभी मानों का योग
B2:B11 में उन कोशिकाओं की संख्या जिनका मान 40 या अधिक है
questions.explanation: COUNTIF counts the cells in a range that meet a condition. Here it counts cells with values >= 40. SUMIF would sum, AVERAGE would average and MAX would give the largest.
questions.explanationHi: COUNTIF किसी सीमा में शर्त पूरी करने वाली कोशिकाओं की गिनती करता है; यहाँ यह उन कोशिकाओं को गिनता है जिनका मान >= 40 है। योग के लिए SUMIF, औसत के लिए AVERAGE और अधिकतम के लिए MAX प्रयुक्त होता है।

questions.question: The decimal number 45 is equal to which binary number?
questions.questionHi: दशमलव संख्या 45 निम्न में से किस द्विआधारी (binary) संख्या के बराबर है?

questions.question: Web-based e-mail such as Gmail, used through a browser without installing software, is a typical example of which cloud service model?
questions.questionHi: ब्राउज़र के माध्यम से बिना सॉफ़्टवेयर इंस्टॉल किए उपयोग की जाने वाली वेब-आधारित ई-मेल सेवा (जैसे Gmail) किस क्लाउड सेवा मॉडल का उदाहरण है?
questions.explanation: In SaaS (Software as a Service) a complete application is delivered over the internet. IaaS gives virtual servers and storage, while PaaS gives a platform for developers to build and deploy applications.
questions.explanationHi: SaaS (Software as a Service) में पूरा एप्लिकेशन इंटरनेट पर उपलब्ध कराया जाता है। IaaS वर्चुअल सर्वर व स्टोरेज देता है, जबकि PaaS डेवलपरों को एप्लिकेशन बनाने और चलाने का प्लेटफ़ॉर्म देता है।

questions.question: In Windows, the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Shift + Esc is used to
questions.questionHi: Windows में कीबोर्ड शॉर्टकट Ctrl + Shift + Esc का उपयोग किसलिए होता है?
optionsHi: Run डायलॉग बॉक्स खोलने के लिए
Task Manager को सीधे खोलने के लिए
कंप्यूटर को लॉक करने के लिए
questions.explanation: Ctrl + Shift + Esc opens Task Manager directly. The Run box is Windows + R, locking is Windows + L, and a screenshot is Print Screen or Windows + Shift + S.
questions.explanationHi: Ctrl + Shift + Esc सीधे Task Manager खोलता है। Run बॉक्स के लिए Windows + R, लॉक के लिए Windows + L और स्क्रीनशॉट के लिए Print Screen या Windows + Shift + S प्रयुक्त होते हैं।

questions.question: In the memory hierarchy, which of the following is the fastest but also the smallest in capacity?
questions.questionHi: मेमोरी पदानुक्रम (memory hierarchy) में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सबसे तेज़ पर क्षमता में सबसे छोटी है?
questions.explanation: CPU registers sit inside the processor and are the fastest and smallest storage, followed by cache, RAM and then secondary storage such as the hard disk, each slower but larger.
questions.explanationHi: CPU रजिस्टर प्रोसेसर के भीतर होते हैं और सबसे तेज़ व सबसे छोटे भंडारण हैं; उसके बाद कैश, RAM और फिर हार्ड डिस्क जैसा द्वितीयक भंडारण आता है, जो क्रमशः धीमा पर बड़ा होता है।

questions.question: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains the provisions on disqualification on grounds of defection (anti-defection law)?
questions.questionHi: भारतीय संविधान की किस अनुसूची में दल-बदल के आधार पर निरर्हता (anti-defection law) के प्रावधान हैं?
questions.explanation: The Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment (1985), deals with disqualification for defection. The Seventh lists Union/State/Concurrent subjects, the Eighth lists languages and the Ninth protects certain laws from judicial review.
questions.explanationHi: 52वें संशोधन (1985) द्वारा जोड़ी गई दसवीं अनुसूची दल-बदल पर निरर्हता से संबंधित है। सातवीं में संघ/राज्य/समवर्ती विषय, आठवीं में भाषाएँ और नौवीं में कुछ कानूनों को न्यायिक समीक्षा से संरक्षण दिया गया है।

questions.question: Which is the highest peak of the Western Ghats and of peninsular India?
questions.questionHi: पश्चिमी घाट और प्रायद्वीपीय भारत की सबसे ऊँची चोटी कौन-सी है?
questions.explanation: Anamudi (about 2,695 m) in the Anamalai hills of Kerala is the highest peak of the Western Ghats and South India. Doddabetta is the highest in the Nilgiris, Mahendragiri is in the Eastern Ghats and Guru Shikhar is in the Aravallis.
questions.explanationHi: केरल की अनामलाई पहाड़ियों में स्थित अनामुडी (लगभग 2,695 मीटर) पश्चिमी घाट और दक्षिण भारत की सबसे ऊँची चोटी है। डोडाबेट्टा नीलगिरि की, महेंद्रगिरि पूर्वी घाट की और गुरु शिखर अरावली की सबसे ऊँची चोटी है।

questions.question: The Indian National Congress declared 'Purna Swaraj' (complete independence) as its goal at which session?
questions.questionHi: भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस ने 'पूर्ण स्वराज' (पूर्ण स्वतंत्रता) को अपना लक्ष्य किस अधिवेशन में घोषित किया?
questions.explanation: At the Lahore session (December 1929), presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, Congress adopted the Purna Swaraj resolution. Karachi 1931 dealt with Fundamental Rights; Calcutta 1928 gave the dominion-status ultimatum; Nagpur 1920 adopted non-cooperation.
questions.explanationHi: जवाहरलाल नेहरू की अध्यक्षता में लाहौर अधिवेशन (दिसंबर 1929) में कांग्रेस ने पूर्ण स्वराज का प्रस्ताव पारित किया। कराची 1931 मौलिक अधिकारों से, कलकत्ता 1928 डोमिनियन स्टेटस की चेतावनी से और नागपुर 1920 असहयोग से संबंधित है।

questions.question: The twinkling of stars is caused by
questions.questionHi: तारों के टिमटिमाने का कारण है
options: polarisation of light by the atmosphere
diffraction of light by the Moon
optionsHi: बादलों द्वारा तारों के प्रकाश का परावर्तन
तारों के प्रकाश का वायुमंडलीय अपवर्तन
questions.explanation: Starlight passes through layers of air of varying, fluctuating density and is refracted continuously, so the apparent position and brightness of the star keep changing, making it twinkle. Planets, being closer, appear as extended sources and do not twinkle noticeably.
questions.explanationHi: तारों का प्रकाश बदलते घनत्व वाली वायु की परतों से गुज़रते हुए लगातार अपवर्तित होता है, जिससे तारे की स्थिति और चमक बदलती रहती है और वह टिमटिमाता है। ग्रह निकट होने से विस्तृत स्रोत जैसे दिखते हैं और स्पष्ट रूप से नहीं टिमटिमाते।

questions.question: The Ravishankar Sagar (Gangrel) dam in Chhattisgarh is built on which river?
questions.questionHi: छत्तीसगढ़ का रविशंकर सागर (गंगरेल) बाँध किस नदी पर बना है?
questions.explanation: Ravishankar Sagar near Dhamtari is built on the Mahanadi, the state's main river. Hasdeo has the Minimata Bango dam, Shivnath is a tributary of the Mahanadi and Indravati flows through Bastar.
questions.explanationHi: धमतरी के पास रविशंकर सागर बाँध राज्य की प्रमुख नदी महानदी पर बना है। हसदेव पर मिनीमाता बांगो बाँध है, शिवनाथ महानदी की सहायक नदी है और इंद्रावती बस्तर से बहती है।
